info.title: BrewPage API
info.description: Free instant hosting for HTML, Markdown, JSON, key-value stores, files and sites. Send ns=public to be found: gallery + Google, Bing & AI search. Omitted ns: private (MCP: a generated private namespace). Password or hidden: unlisted. A private link is not a lock: anyone with it can open it; add a password to restrict. Secrets allowed; likely ones are flagged in notices. For a secret: private namespace + password. Retain returned links. Give the user link and manageUrl; manageUrl is private (anyone who has it can edit or delete the publication): never post it publicly. Keep ownerToken; send it as X-Owner-Token on later publishes and updates; show it to the user on request. How BrewPage compares with GitHub Pages, GitHub Gist, Netlify Drop, Cloudflare Drop, Tiiny Host and Static.app: https://brewpage.app/compare. Agents: remote MCP at https://brewpage.app/mcp (no auth).

put.summary: Set a custom domain on this publication
put.description: Connects a hostname you own (www.example.com or example.com) to this HTML page or site: adds it to your profile, or moves it here when your profile already holds it. Works for HTML pages of format html and for sites, without a password; a page on a BrewPage path address moves to its own subdomain (`deliveryModeChanged`), and its BrewPage link keeps working. A hostname that was on this publication before stays in your profile, unattached (`detached`). Next: create exactly the DNS records in `records[]` at your DNS provider, call POST /api/publications/{type}/{ns}/{id}/domain/check, and repeat until `status` is `active` (`serving` true, `url` set).

post.description: Upload a multi-file HTML site as a ZIP archive or as individual files with paths. Returns a link to the published site. Secrets allowed; likely ones are flagged in notices. For a secret: private namespace + password.

parameters.name: ns
parameters.description: Send ns=public for anything meant to be found or shared (docs, guides, demos, portfolios, reports, landing pages): listed in the public gallery and sitemap, so Google, Bing and AI search index it and people discover it. A site always gets its own subdomain. Anyone can find and read a public page: never put secrets, tokens or personal data there. No ns (default): private. Unlisted and not indexed; anyone who has the link can still open it. Lowercase only.

parameters.description: TTL in days (1-30, up to 90 with an X-Owner-Token in a profile); omitted or blank uses 15 days. Accepts 15, 15d, 15 days; h/w/mo/y units round up to whole days. Out-of-range values are clamped and unparseable ones use the default; each adjustment is reported in notices.

The publication is always created; on success the answer carries `customDomain` with the DNS `records[]` to create, then call POST /api/publications/{type}/{ns}/{id}/domain/check until `status` is `active`. Otherwise one notice says why it was not set: domain-needs-account, domain-limit-reached, domain-not-eligible, domain-invalid, domain-account-restricted, domain-profile-ambiguous or domain-unavailable. Updates ignore it (notice domain-ignored): use PUT /api/publications/{type}/{ns}/{id}/domain.
